summary: Final tokens truncated after QUIC path-migration + idle-probe; resume emits duplicate 'end' metadata
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports that streaming completions cut off the last 2–6 tokens when a mobile client performs a QUIC path migration triggered by an idle probe. The client reconnects and the resume contains duplicate 'end' metadata frames while the final JSON envelope is split across chunks, leading to invalid application-level assembly.

Impact:
- Certain production users at Acme Retail receive truncated completions in chat assistant flows; high business impact for enterprise SLOs.
- Affects ~0.4% of streaming sessions during observed window; customers report user-visible truncation and occasional parse errors.

Environment:
- Production (us-east) - Hosted Redwood API, customers on enterprise plan with region pinning.
- Not observed in staging.

Steps to reproduce (from customer repro):
1) Start a long streaming completion (>512 tokens) from mobile app behind NAT and cellular->wifi handover enabled.
2) Let session go idle for ~45s (idle probe fires).
3) Trigger QUIC path migration (simulate network interface change).
4) Client resumes stream; client SDK reports reconnection and attempts resume with last seen offset.

Expected behavior:
- Resume restores cached prefix, continues streaming remaining tokens and emits single end metadata event.
- Final JSON envelope stays intact and is parseable.

Actual behavior:
- Final tokens truncated (2–6 tokens).
- Duplicate 'end' metadata events observed in the resumed stream.
- Final JSON envelope split across two chunks; client-side assembler fails and emits parse error in ~15% of affected cases.

Attached logs and artifacts:
- Raw SSE transcript (redacted): https://s3.redwood-internal/acme/sse-transcript-2026-03-09.log
- TCP/QUIC flow trace: https://telemetry.redwood/internal/flows/flow-9812
- Customer SDK trace (session id): acme-ss-87e4
logs: 2026-03-09T18:42:12Z serving-runtime: session=acme-ss-87e4 idle_probe=45s path_migrate=quic token_count_before=513 token_count_after=507
investigation_notes: 03-09 18:45 - Reproduced locally with QUIC path migration emulator: observed KV cache invalidation on the serving node coincident with upstream connection rebind.

03-09 19:05 - Hypothesis: proxy (envoy) rebind during path migration races with serving-runtime session state reconciliation, causing one resume path to send a trimmed final frame while another sends an 'end' marker (duplicates).

03-10 09:10 - Trace-level sampling shows resume messages arriving out-of-order at the runtime (sequence numbers 1021, 1023 with missing 1022); suggests packet reordering / retransmit masks the final payload.
short_term_workaround: Advise customer to disable aggressive mobile path-migration during critical streaming sessions (client-side toggle).
Enable server-side conservative idle probe for this customer tenant: increase keepalive to 120s (tenant override) to reduce path migration windows.
resolution_notes: 03-11 - Hotfix deployed to api-gateway: ensure resume handshake includes monotonic resume nonce and server-side re-assembly guard to accept duplicate 'end' markers without truncation.

03-11 - Serving-runtime patch (PR #2487) adds short-lived KV-cache grace on connection handoff to allow inflight token forwarding. Deployed to canary (us-east-a) and rolled to 25% traffic. Monitoring shows truncation rate dropped from 0.4% to 0.02% for canary traffic.
Follow-up: full rollout planned after 48h of canary monitoring, additional tests for HTTP/3 QUIC path migration scenarios added to CI.
next_steps: Complete full rollout if canary metrics remain stable (owner: Miguel Alvarez).
Add targeted e2e test in mobile SDK suite that simulates interface handover + idle probe to prevent regressions.
Document tenant override knobs in runbook and inform CS/SE teams.
